change.describe: branch `ao-replay/9076` of ao-replay-9076 against f10c84ce6b2c3ed2b0e49913f58998063a6a600e (merge-base f10c84c)
change.title: ao-replay/9076
change.description:
fix(devices): restart the device hub when a simulator boots outside AO
fix(devices): catch outside reboots nobody was watching
change.author: Prasad-D-Ware

findings.title: Hub replacement does not wait for in-flight hub work, and takes down every device's stream
findings.body: `restartHub` cancels the hub (line 1161) and sets `p.hub = nil` (1167-1169) with no regard for other calls using it. `Hub()` then answers "device support is not running" (line 581) until `EnsureReady` finishes, which can take up to the 2 minute context at 1171. A `Boot` for a different simulator or session that is mid-flight (`/api/devices/boot`, grid start, `resetSimulatorHelper`, lines 986-1015) then fails. On that failure `Boot` tries `p.Shutdown` through the same dead hub (1024), so a simulator it powered on can be left running with no lease. The user sees an error, not silent corruption. One outside boot of simulator X also drops the streams of every other simulator and emulator. Consider skipping the replacement while any `Boot` is running (`ownBoots` is non-empty), or retrying the replacement afterwards. Also say in the NoteBooted doc that every viewer reconnects, not just the rebooted device's.

findings.title: No compile-time assertion that Provider implements DeviceBootWatcher
findings.body: `devices.Service.LiveLease` finds the watcher with a runtime type assertion (`service.go:905`). If `NoteBooted`'s signature drifts, the assertion fails silently and outside-boot detection stops, with no compile error. Add `var _ ports.DeviceBootWatcher = (*Provider)(nil)` next to the existing `var _ ports.DeviceProvider` at line 110.

findings.title: The real restartHub is never exercised
findings.body: Every new test replaces `p.replaceHub` with a fake that only clears `replacingHub`. `restartHub` (provider.go:1148-1180) has the riskiest logic in the change: cancel without revive, the 5 s wait on `done`, clearing `p.hub`, `EnsureReady`, and `reviveHub` when `EnsureReady` fails. None of it has a test. A test could use a `hubProcess` whose `cancel` closes `done`, and a failing `lookPath` so `EnsureReady` errors. It would assert that `replacingHub` is reset and that `reviveHub` runs on failure but not on `errProviderClosed`.

findings.title: Asynchronous recordBoots at hub start can overwrite a newer boot id
findings.body: The goroutine at lines 254-258 runs simctl and then writes `p.bootIDs` for every simulator unconditionally (lines 1131-1136). It runs concurrently with `Boot`. If its simctl read happens before a boot that `Boot` then records via `recordBoots(..., device.ID)` (line 1038), and its write lands after that, `bootIDs` ends up holding the older id. The next `NoteBooted` then sees a changed boot with `ownBoots` already cleared, and restarts the hub for a boot AO made itself. The window is small. Is it worth recording synchronously, or only writing ids for simulators not yet in the map?

contracts.action: LiveLease tells the provider which boot a running leased simulator is on (NoteBooted)
contracts.equivalent_path: Boot (provider.go:955) / resetSimulatorHelper, which already replaces the stream helper for boots that go through AO
contracts.before_after: Before: only AO-initiated boots got a fresh stream helper. After: LiveLease, which viewers poll, passes the listed device (with BootID from simctl lastUsedAt) to NoteBooted. A change on a boot with no `ownBoots` mark replaces the hub in a goroutine. It runs only for a running device and a provider that implements DeviceBootWatcher.
contracts.visible_effect: After an outside reboot, viewers lose their streams, reconnect to the new hub, and touch input works. The log gets an Info line.
contracts.failure_mode: If simctl is unavailable, BootID is empty and NoteBooted returns early, which leaves the old behaviour. If EnsureReady fails during the replacement, restartHub logs a Warn and starts reviveHub, which retries with backoff. In-flight Boots for other devices fail loudly during the replacement window.

contracts.action: Bounds on the new waits: the recordBoots goroutine after hub start, the recordBoots call at the end of Boot, and restartHub
contracts.equivalent_path: The existing deadline-bounded stream wait in Boot (awaitLiveStream) and the 2 min EnsureReady context in reviveHub (provider.go:559)
contracts.before_after: Each wait has its own limit. The recordBoots goroutine in EnsureReady is limited to 30 s from p.life. The recordBoots in Boot is limited to 15 s on a context detached from the boot's cancellation, so it adds at most 15 s after bootTimeout. restartHub waits 5 s for hub.done, then runs EnsureReady with a 2 min context from p.life. All of these use process.CommandContext, so simctl is killed at the limit. LiveLease and viewers never block on the replacement because it runs in a goroutine.
contracts.visible_effect: Worst case, `ao device open` returns up to 15 s later than before if simctl hangs after the stream is up. Otherwise nothing waits on the replacement.
contracts.failure_mode: A recordBoots failure leaves bootIDs stale. NoteBooted updates bootIDs on every look, including during a boot, so a spurious restart happens only if no viewer looked during the boot.

summary: The change detects a simulator that rebooted outside AO by comparing simctl's `lastUsedAt` between looks, and restarts the device hub when that happens. I read the code paths and found no blockers. The new tests mostly assert what they claim. One test group fakes `replaceHub`, so the real `restartHub` is untested. I also flag three smaller points. A hub replacement disrupts in-flight Boots and every device's stream. There is no compile-time check that `Provider` implements `DeviceBootWatcher`. The hub-start `recordBoots` goroutine can race with `Boot`'s own recording.
